chunks: But they called him a liar and hamstrung her. So God obliterated them for their crime, and (destroyed) all of them alike.

key_terms.فَسَوَّاهَا: and made them all alike / destroyed them uniformly
key_terms.فَكَذَّبُوهُ: they called him a liar / denied him

ai.seo_question: What happened to the people of Thamud when they killed the camel?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the 'she-camel' (Naqat) is viewed not merely as an animal but as a divine sign (Ayah) whose sacrificial killing by the Thamud symbolizes the rejection of prophetic authority and the subsequent loss of divine favor. The term 'damada' implies a sudden, overwhelming destruction that leveled their societal structure, serving as a cautionary archetype for those who transgress divine boundaries despite clear omens. This narrative underscores the Shia emphasis on the tangible connection between moral obedience to the Prophet and the preservation of communal stability.
